**Short answer:** Under the law in force on 15 January 2026, the documents suggest the app company probably cannot charge you a card fee for paying rent, but the position is not fully settled. The documents also don't say who the fee goes to is irrelevant, and they don't define key terms.

## What the law says

- **The agent must offer a no-extra-cost option.** The rental provider or agent must ensure a rent payment method that incurs no additional costs (other than the renter's own bank or account fees) is reasonably available to you. The penalty is 80 penalty units for a natural person or 400 for a body corporate [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- **You must be told about fees first.** The provider or agent must give you information about any costs, including third-party transaction fees, before you consent to a payment method [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- **Charges for electronic payment facilities are restricted.** A person must not demand or receive a charge from a renter in relation to the use of any other electronic payment facility for payment of rent (penalty: 60 penalty units) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). This wording is broad enough to cover a card fee, but the documents don't say whether a card is an "electronic payment facility" in this sense.
- **Fees for rent payment are restricted, with a carve-out.** A business that is not a provider, provider's agent or authorised deposit-taking institution must not demand or receive a fee for a prescribed matter relating to paying rent [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). The payments company is not one of the excluded persons [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). However, the prescribed matters are listed in regulation 21C, which only takes effect on 31 March 2026 [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf). That regulation excludes "payment surcharge fees permitted under any other Act" [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf). The documents do not identify any Act that permits such surcharges.
- **Agreement terms.** A term requiring rent to be paid in advance by a method with additional costs (other than bank or account fees) is a prohibited term [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf).

**Version and date:** On 15 January 2026, the *Residential Tenancies Act 1997* (Version 111, in force from 25 November 2025 to 29 June 2026) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf) and the *Residential Tenancies Regulations 2021* (Version 005, in force from 25 November 2025 to 9 February 2026) [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf) apply. Regulation 21C is not yet in effect on this date [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf).

## Does it matter who gets the fee?

The documents suggest it matters for which rule applies, but the obligations point in the same direction:

- **If the agent receives any part of the fee,** the agent is directly bound by the no-extra-cost duty and the charge restriction [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- **If only the app company keeps the fee,** the restriction on charging for rent payment still applies to it as a business that is not an excluded person [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). Its liability for a rent payment fee depends on regulation 21C, which is not in force yet [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf).
- The agent still has the duty to ensure a no-extra-cost method is reasonably available [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf), even if a third party charges the fee.

## What you can do or ask

1. **Ask the agent in writing** what costs the card option carries, as the agent must disclose these before you choose it [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
2. **Ask for the bank transfer option to be made available** and confirm that the agent is required to ensure a no-extra-cost method is reasonably available [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). The documents do not define "reasonably available," so a slower method may or may not meet this test.
3. **Ask for a receipt** for each rent payment. You can request one, and it must be given within 5 business days of the request if you don't pay in person [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
4. **Check your agreement.** If it requires a payment method with extra costs, it may be a prohibited term [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf).

The documents don't set out how to enforce these rights or complain about a breach beyond the penalties mentioned above. If you need that, you'll need to check other sources.

**Short answer:** Based on the Residential Tenancies Act 1997, Authorised Version No. 088 (in force 2 July to 3 December 2019, so it applies on 15 October 2019) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf), you may be able to end the agreement before moving in, and the landlord must fix the defects. The documents do not clearly support a rent reduction. They say you need not pay rent for the period before you can move in, but that is not the same as a general rent cut.

**What the law says**

- **Landlord's duty on the handover day:** The landlord must ensure that on the day you are to enter occupation, the premises are vacant and reasonably clean. You are not required to move in if they do not comply [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- **Rent before moving in:** If the premises do not comply, you are not required to pay rent from the agreed occupation day until the day you actually move in [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- **Duty to maintain:** The landlord must ensure the premises are maintained in good repair [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- **Mould and damp:** The Act's definition of urgent repairs includes "any fault or damage that makes rented premises... unsafe or insecure", including "the presence of mould or damp caused by or related to the building structure" [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). This version also contains amending text that changes this definition, but the documents do not clearly show whether that amendment was in operation on 15 October 2019.
- **Condition report:** Before you enter occupation, the landlord must give you two copies of a condition report stating the state of repair and general condition of the premises [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). If you are not given one, you may complete one and give it to the landlord between inspecting the premises and 5 business days after entering occupation [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).

**Your options**

1. **Cancel:** Under section 226, a tenancy terminates if the tenant has not entered into possession and has given the landlord a notice of termination on the ground that the premises are "not in good repair" or "unfit for human habitation" (among other grounds) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). Whether collecting the keys counts as "entering into possession" is not addressed in the documents, so this needs checking before you rely on it.
   - Alternatively, section 238 allows a tenant to give a notice of intention to vacate if the premises are "unfit for human habitation" or destroyed or unsafe. The notice may specify a termination date that is the date it is given or a later date [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). Section 238 is not limited to premises you have not yet entered, but its application to your situation is not confirmed.

2. **Ask for repairs:**
   - Notify the landlord in writing. A renter must give written notice "as soon as practicable after becoming aware of" damage [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
   - **Urgent repairs:** If the landlord cannot or does not carry out urgent repairs after you have taken reasonable steps to arrange them, you may arrange them. The landlord must reimburse the reasonable cost [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). The documents do not say whether this applies before you have moved in.
   - **Non-urgent repairs:** You may apply to the Director to investigate if you have given written notice and the landlord has not carried out the repairs within 14 days [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). You may apply to the Tribunal (VCAT) for an order requiring specified repairs [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).

3. **Ask for lower rent:** The documents do not provide a direct route to reduce rent for defects. The Tribunal can make a rent order that considers the state of repair and general condition of the premises [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf), which may be relevant if you pursue a rent dispute. The only specific rent protection in the documents is the rent-free period before you move in, described above [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). Rent paid into the Rent Special Account is linked to repair notices, but the documents do not clearly show how this applies before occupation [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).

**What the documents don't cover**

- Whether you have "entered into possession" by collecting keys (this affects section 226).
- How the lease terms affect your rights.
- Whether the urgent repair and rent account provisions apply before you move in.
- Whether the amendments changing the urgent repairs definition were in operation on 15 October 2019.

Because cancelling a lease can have significant consequences, consider getting advice from Consumer Affairs Victoria or a tenancy lawyer before serving any notice. This suggestion is general and not from the documents.

### What the law says about entry

- **Who can enter and when:** A provider or their agent may enter, with any necessary persons, at any time agreed with the renter if the renter consented within 7 days before entry. Otherwise, entry is allowed between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. on any day except a public holiday, with notice [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- **Notice:** For a duty under the Act, such as a smoke alarm check, at least 24 hours' notice is required [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). Seven days' notice is more than enough. The notice must be in writing, state why entry is wanted, and be given by post or delivered personally between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). Your 10 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. weekday window falls within the permitted hours.
- **Your duty:** A renter must permit entry that complies with the Act, but a renter can apply to the Tribunal (VCAT) for an order specifying or limiting when entry may occur [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- **Conduct:** The person entering must act reasonably and must not stay longer than necessary without your consent [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- **Smoke alarms:** The provider must ensure smoke alarms are working, have batteries, and are tested at least once every 12 months. Mains-powered smoke alarms must be tested, repaired or replaced by a suitably qualified person [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).

### Do you have to be there?

The retrieved excerpts don't say whether a renter must be present during an entry. They only say you must permit entry that follows the Act's procedure [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf)[[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf). Having a key does not in itself grant entry rights. The entry must still meet the notice, timing and manner requirements above. The documents don't address whether you can ask for a different time, other than through a VCAT application.

### Can they charge $90?

The retrieved documents contain no provision for a rebooking fee for a missed entry. I can't say whether it is lawful, and I'm not able to answer that from these sources. The Act does prohibit a provider from demanding fees for consent to assignment or sub-letting [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf), but that does not cover this situation.

### What you can do

1. **Check the notice:** Confirm it is in writing, states the reason for entry, and was delivered properly [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).

## What the law says

- **Where and how rent is paid:** Rent is payable at the place specified in the agreement, or at the rented premises if none is specified. Otherwise it is payable in the manner specified in the agreement [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- **Changing the payment method:** The landlord and renter, *by agreement*, may change the manner in which rent is payable [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). The Act does not allow the owner to change it unilaterally.
- **Costs:** Before you consent to a payment method, the provider or agent must tell you about any costs you may incur by using it, including third-party transaction fees and electronic payment facility fees [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- **Fee-free option:** The provider or agent must ensure a payment method that incurs no additional costs (other than your bank or account fees) is reasonably available [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). Centrepay must also be permitted [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- **Receipts:** For rent paid other than in person, you can request a written receipt, which must be given within 5 business days. It must be signed and state your name and the rented premises, the date, the period paid for, the amount, and that the payment is for rent [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- **Contact changes:** The provider must notify you in writing of any change to the agent's or provider's contact details within 7 days of the change [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- **Bond:** The bond must be lodged with the Residential Tenancies Bond Authority within 10 business days after it is received, and the provider must give you a bond lodgment form [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). If the provider assigns or transfers their rights and duties to another person and a bond has been paid, both must notify the Authority within 5 days, and the provider must give you a copy of that notice [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).

1. **Check your lease.** Look for the clause on where and how rent is paid. If it names the agent's account, the owner cannot simply substitute theirs without an agreed change [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
2. **Ask for the change in writing.** Ask the agent to confirm, in writing, that the owner is now the rental provider and that you agree to the new payment method. Don't rely on a phone call or an unverified message with new bank details.
3. **Confirm the account details.** Check that the account name matches the owner named in the agreement or in the written notice, and verify the details through a channel you already trust (for example, by calling a number you already have, not one in the message).
4. **Ask about costs.** Find out whether the new method carries fees. You're entitled to that information before you consent [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
5. **Ask for a receipt.** Every rent payment should produce a receipt that meets the content requirements above [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
6. **Check the bond.** Confirm the bond is held by the Authority. That form is for agreements of more than 5 years, so it may not match your lease. Check which form your agreement uses.

The documents don't say how to verify a bank account or whether a change of manager needs a new agreement. They also don't cover what to do if the change turns out to be a scam. For those points, contact Consumer Affairs Victoria on 1300 558 181, which is listed in the regulations form [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-06/21-3sra002%20authorised.pdf).

- *Residential Tenancies Regulations 2021*, file "rt-regs-2021-v005-2025-11-25.pdf", version 005, in force 25 Nov 2025 to 9 Feb 2026 [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf).

## What the law says

**1. A no-extra-cost option must be available.**
- The provider or their agent must ensure a rent payment method with no additional costs is reasonably available to you. Bank fees or account fees on your own account don't count as additional costs [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- Your free bank transfer option seems to meet this. The Act doesn't define "reasonably available", and it doesn't say whether a slower method still qualifies. The documents don't answer that.
- Electronic funds transfer is a prescribed method that must be permitted [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf)[[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf).

**2. You must be told about fees before you agree.**
- The provider or agent must give you information about any costs you may incur by using a particular payment method before you consent to it. The Act expressly lists "third party transaction fees" and "any other electronic payment facility fees" [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).

**3. A charge for using an electronic payment facility is prohibited.**
- Section 51(3) says a person must not demand or receive from a renter a charge for "the establishment or use of direct debit facilities or any other electronic payment facility for payment of rent". The penalty is 60 penalty units [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- A card-paying app arguably falls within this. The documents don't say whether a card surcharge counts as such a charge, so I can't say definitively that it does.
- Section 42(7) expressly contemplates "third party transaction fees". That sits uneasily with section 51(3), and the documents don't reconcile the two.

**4. A newer fee ban isn't operating yet on this date.**
- Section 51A bans a business (other than the provider, the provider's agent, or a bank) from demanding or receiving a fee for a "prescribed matter" relating to the payment of rent [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- The regulation that lists the prescribed matters, including "rent payment (other than payment surcharge fees permitted under any other Act)", has effect only on and after 31 March 2026 [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf).
- So on 15 January 2026 the retrieved documents don't show this ban applying. My reading is that the section depends on that regulation, but the documents don't say so expressly.

## Does it matter whether the app company or the agent gets the fee?

- **Now (15 Jan 2026):** On its face, section 51(3) applies to "a person", so it doesn't distinguish between the payments company and the agent [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). The documents don't say more about how it applies to a third-party payments company.
- **From 31 March 2026:** It will matter. Section 51A catches a business such as a payments company but expressly excludes the provider and the agent [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf)[[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf). A fee kept by the agent wouldn't fall under section 51A, though sections 42 and 51 would still apply to it [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). A fee charged by the app company would fall under it, subject to the carve-out for surcharges permitted under another Act [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf). That carve-out is not explained in the documents.
- A later version of the regulations (version 005 ends 9 Feb 2026) may change this. I don't have it.

## What you can do

- **Use the free bank transfer.** You're entitled to a no-additional-cost method [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- **Ask for the fee in writing before you consent.** The agent must disclose any fee, including third-party transaction fees, before you agree to the method [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- **Raise section 51(3) with the agent.** Ask them to confirm in writing that the card fee isn't a charge for use of an electronic payment facility.
- **Check your agreement.** It lists the provider's preferred payment methods and notes that a fee-free method must be permitted [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf).

The documents don't cover how to complain or enforce these rules, so I can't advise on that from them.

answer:
## What the law says

I used the **Residential Tenancies Act 1997, Authorised Version No. 088** (incorporating amendments as at 2 July 2019). The file is titled "rta-1997-v088-2019-07-02.pdf" and was in force from 2 July 2019 to 3 December 2019 [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). That covers 15 October 2019.

- **Landlord's duty:** a landlord must ensure the rented premises are maintained in good repair (s 68(1)) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- **Ending the agreement before moving in:** a tenancy agreement terminates if the tenant has not entered into possession and has given the landlord a notice of termination on the ground that the premises are, among other things, (a) not in good repair, (b) unfit for human habitation, or (f) for any other reason unavailable for occupation (s 226) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- **Definition of tenant:** "tenant" includes a person to whom premises are to be let under a proposed tenancy agreement, so the repair rights below should apply to you before you move in [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).

## What you can do

**1. Cancel**
- You can give the landlord a notice of termination under s 226, citing "not in good repair", "unfit for human habitation" and/or "unavailable for occupation" [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- It only works if you have **not entered into possession**. The Act text I retrieved doesn't say whether collecting the keys counts as possession, so don't move in or stay there.
- The retrieved text doesn't set out a required form or notice period for this notice, so I can't tell you either.
- Another route is to agree with the landlord to end the agreement (s 217) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).

**2. Ask for repairs**
- **Urgent repairs:** these are a defined list. It includes a serious roof leak, flooding or serious flood damage, and "any fault or damage that makes rented premises… unsafe or insecure" [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). If the rot or damp falls into one of those, you can arrange the repairs yourself once you have taken reasonable steps to get the landlord to do them and couldn't (s 72). You must give 14 days' written notice of the repairs and cost. The landlord must reimburse the reasonable cost, up to $1000 or any higher prescribed amount (s 72(2)) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). You can also apply to the Tribunal for an urgent repairs order, which must be heard within 2 business days (s 73) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). Whether damp, mould or rotting timber is "urgent" depends on the facts. The documents don't say.
- **Non-urgent repairs:**
  1. Give the landlord written notice.
  2. If the repairs aren't done within 14 days, apply to the Director to investigate (s 74).
  3. If you're still unsatisfied, apply to the Tribunal within 60 days of the Director's report. You can apply without the report if you haven't received it within 90 days of applying for it (s 75).
  4. The Tribunal can order specified repairs and set a deadline (s 76) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- **Rent into the Rent Special Account:** after giving repair notice, you can ask the Tribunal to let you pay rent into this account while the landlord fails to repair (s 77) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- **Exception:** if the house is subject to a declaration under s 64 of the Housing Act 1983, you can't use ss 72–75 (s 80) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).

**3. Lower rent**
- I found **no provision in this version that gives a direct right to a rent reduction** for pre-move-in defects.
- The only provision that excuses rent is s 65(3). It applies if the premises aren't vacant and reasonably clean on the agreed day. In that case you needn't pay rent from the agreed occupation day until you actually move in (s 65(2)–(3)) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). The documents don't say whether mould counts as "reasonably clean", so I can't say it applies.
- The excessive-rent process lets the Tribunal consider "the state of repair and general condition" of the premises (s 47(3)(b)). But you reach it through a Director complaint about reduced services or a rent increase notice (ss 45–46) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf), and neither fits your situation clearly.

## Practical points
- If you paid a bond, the landlord must give you two copies of a condition report before you occupy. You must return one within 3 business days after entering occupation (s 35) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). A report signed by both parties is conclusive evidence of the premises' condition, unless you endorse your disagreement (s 36) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). Record the damp, mould and rot on it and take dated photos.
- The same file contains endnote text from an amending Act that uses "renter" and "residential rental provider". It includes a "reasonably fit and suitable condition" duty and a "rental minimum standards" ground in a new s 91L [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). That is amending text, not the operative body of this version, so I haven't relied on it for 15 October 2019.

If you want to cancel, send the s 226 notice in writing before you take possession. Check the exact notice requirements with Consumer Affairs Victoria or a tenancy advice service, because the documents I retrieved don't cover them.

**Documents used:** the *Residential Tenancies Act 1997* (title "rta-1997-v111-2025-11-25.pdf", dated 25 Nov 2025, version 111, in force 25 Nov 2025 to 29 Jun 2026) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). I also used the *Residential Tenancies Regulations 2021* (title "rt-regs-2021-v005-2025-11-25.pdf", dated 25 Nov 2025, version 005, in force 25 Nov 2025 to 9 Feb 2026) [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf). Both were in force on 3 December 2025. The documents give version numbers (111 and 005) but not an "Authorised Version No." label as such.

## What the law says

**Is the entry allowed?**
- The rental provider has a duty to make sure smoke alarms are working and tested at least once every 12 months [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). This is in s 68AA of the Act.
- Entry is allowed where it is needed so the rental provider can carry out a duty under the Act (s 86(1)(c)) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- That entry must be between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. on any day except a public holiday, with at least 24 hours' notice given under s 88 (s 85(b)(iii)) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- Your notice gave 7 days and a weekday window of 10 am to 12:30 pm, so on its face it is within those limits. Treating a smoke alarm check as a s 86(1)(c) purpose is my reading of the Act. The text doesn't name smoke alarm checks in s 86.
- The notice must also be in writing, state why the agent wants to enter, and be posted or hand-delivered between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. (s 88) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- If the alarm is mains-powered, the testing must be done by a suitably qualified person (s 68AA(5)) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).

**Do you have to be home?**
- The Act says a renter has a duty to *permit* a person exercising a right of entry in accordance with the Division to enter (s 89(1)) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). The Regulations' standard-form summary says the renter must allow entry where the rental provider has followed proper procedure [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf).
- The retrieved text does not say the renter must be present. It also does not say whether an agent may use their own key when the renter is out. It only says entry must be in a reasonable manner and no longer than necessary (s 87) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- So I can't confirm from these documents that you must be home. I also can't confirm that you may refuse an agent using a key, as long as the entry follows the notice rules above.

**Can they charge $90?**
- I found nothing in the retrieved text that authorises, or expressly prohibits, a "rebooking fee" for missing an inspection. The documents do not answer this.
- The only charge-related provisions I retrieved are s 51 (premiums, key money, and charges for a prospective renter's inspection) and s 51A (application and rent-payment fees) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). Neither covers this situation.
- One possibly relevant point is that the Regulations list as a prohibited term "a term which imposes fees for, or delegates, safety-related maintenance that is the responsibility of the residential rental provider" (reg 11(f)) [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf). Smoke alarm testing is the provider's duty [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). Whether that applies to a missed-appointment fee is unclear from these documents.

## What you can do
- **Ask the agent to identify the legal basis for the $90 fee**, and check whether it is in your lease.
- **Ask for a different time or agree one.** The Act allows entry at any time you agree if you consented within 7 days before the entry (s 85(a)) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- **Apply to the Tribunal** for an order specifying or limiting when entry may occur (s 89(2)–(3)) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- **Apply to the Tribunal for an order** restraining entry for a specified period if an agent exercises entry without complying with the Division (s 91) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). Entering otherwise than in accordance with the Division, without reasonable excuse, is an offence (s 91A) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- **Seek advice** from Consumer Affairs Victoria or a community legal service on the fee question, since these documents don't settle it.

## What the law says

- **Change of manager.** If an agent acts for the rental provider, the provider must give you the agent's name, address and contact details. If there is no agent, the provider must give their own full name, address for service and an emergency phone number. Any change to that information must be notified to you in writing within 7 days after the change (s 66(2)–(4)) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). The standard lease form repeats this [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-06/21-3sra002%20authorised.pdf).
- **How rent is paid.** Rent is payable in the manner specified in your agreement, at the place specified there (s 42(1)–(2)) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). The provider and renter, by agreement, may change the manner in which rent is payable (s 42(6)) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). The standard form has a "Payment details" section where the provider lists the payment method [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-06/21-3sra002%20authorised.pdf).
- **Costs and fee-free options.**
  - The provider or their agent must make a payment method with no additional cost, other than your own bank fees, reasonably available to you (s 42(4)) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
  - They must tell you about any costs of a payment method before you consent to it (s 42(7)) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- **Receipts.**
  - A person who receives rent must give you a written receipt. It is due immediately if you pay in person. If you don't pay in person, it is due within 5 business days if you request it when you pay (s 43(1)) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
  - The receipt must be signed and must state your name and the premises, the date, the period paid, the amount, and that it is for rent (s 43(3)) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
  - If no receipt is required, the recipient must keep a record for 12 months. You can request a copy, which must be provided within 5 business days (s 43(2), (2A)) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- **Your bond.**
  - The provider must lodge it with the Residential Tenancies Bond Authority within 10 business days of receiving it (s 406) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
  - The Authority must send you a receipt within 7 days of receiving it (s 407(1)) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
  - If you have no receipt within 15 business days, you can notify the Authority (s 409(1)) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
  - The Authority's receipt must show the bond amount and date, the renters, the premises, the name and address of the rental provider, and the bond number (reg 94) [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-06/21-3sra002%20authorised.pdf).
  - If the provider transfers their rights and duties under the agreement to someone else, they and the new person must notify the Authority within 5 days. The provider must give you a copy of that notice (s 424) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).

## What you can do or ask

1. **Ask for the change in writing.** Request written notice of who is now managing, with their full name, address for service and emergency number, as s 66 requires [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). Check it covers the change the agent described and that it came within 7 days.

Ask for the new account details to be set out in writing as an agreed change, since s 42(6) allows the manner of payment to change by agreement [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).

## Law applying on 15 October 2019

The applicable document is **Residential Tenancies Act 1997, Authorised Version 088, in force from 2 July 2019 to 3 December 2019**. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf)

Because you have not moved your belongings in or stayed there, the Act’s “before possession” rule appears relevant. Under section 226, a tenancy agreement terminates if the tenant has not entered into possession and gives the landlord a **notice of termination** stating that the premises are:

- not in good repair;
- unfit for human habitation;
- unsafe;
- not vacant;
- not legally available for residential use; or
- otherwise unavailable for occupation. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf)

The landlord must ensure that, on the agreed occupation day, the premises are vacant and reasonably clean. You are not required to enter premises that do not meet that requirement, and you do not have to pay rent for the period before you actually enter into occupation if the premises do not comply. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf) The landlord must also maintain the premises in good repair. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf)

## What you can do or ask

1. **Cancel/terminate the tenancy:**  
   You can give the landlord a notice of termination under section 226, relying on the premises being **not in good repair** or, if the condition is sufficiently serious, **unfit for human habitation** or otherwise unavailable for occupation. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf) The documents do not state a required notice form or specify whether keys alone amount to entering into possession, so retain evidence that you had not moved in or occupied the house.

2. **Ask for repairs:**  
   You can notify the landlord in writing and ask for the damp, mould and rotting timber to be repaired. The landlord’s duty is to keep the premises in good repair. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf) For non-urgent repairs, if the landlord does not act within **14 days** after written notice, you may apply to the Director to investigate; after receiving the Director’s report, you may apply to the Tribunal for an order requiring specified repairs. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf)

   If the rotting timber or another defect makes the premises **unsafe**, it may fall within “urgent repairs”; the Act includes “any fault or damage that makes rented premises unsafe or insecure.” [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf) The documents do not specifically classify damp or mould as urgent repairs.

3. **Ask for lower rent:**  
   The retrieved provisions do **not** give a general right to reduce the agreed rent merely because defects are discovered before occupation. The excessive-rent process applies where the landlord has reduced or withdrawn services, facilities or other items, or where the tenant receives a notice of a rent increase; it is not stated to cover an initial rent reduction for these defects. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf) You can ask the landlord to agree to a lower rent, but the documents do not establish that you can require it.

Do not simply stop paying rent after entering into occupation: the specific pre-occupation rent protection applies only for the period before you actually enter into occupation when the premises do not comply with section 65. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf)

## What the law says

On **8 November 2022**, the applicable law was the **Residential Tenancies Act 1997, Authorised Version 101 (in force from 7 September 2022)** [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf), and the **Residential Tenancies Regulations 2021, Authorised Version 002 (in force from 1 June 2022)** [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-06/21-3sra002%20authorised.pdf).

- Rent must generally be paid in the manner specified in the residential rental agreement. The rental provider and renter may change that manner **by agreement**. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf)
- If the agency stops acting for the owner, the rental provider must give you written notice of the change in the relevant information **within 7 days**. If there is no agent, that notice must include the owner’s **full name and address for service of documents**, plus an **emergency telephone number for urgent repairs**. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf)
- The agreement’s payment section should identify the available rent-payment methods and payment details. It must provide at least one payment method with no additional cost other than your own bank or account fees. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf)[[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-06/21-3sra002%20authorised.pdf)

## What you should do or ask before paying

1. **Check the signed lease**: confirm the stated rental provider, payment method, account details and first-rent due date. A new bank account is not automatically the agreed payment method; changing the payment manner requires agreement. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf)[[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-06/21-3sra002%20authorised.pdf)

2. **Ask for written confirmation** from the agency and owner that:
   - the agency has ceased acting;
   - the owner is now managing the tenancy;
   - the owner’s full name and address for service; and
   - the urgent-repairs emergency telephone number.  
   These are the details the owner must provide when there is no agent, and changes must be notified in writing within 7 days. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf)

3. **Independently verify the new account details** with the owner or agency using contact details already appearing in your signed lease—not merely by replying to the message containing the new bank details. The retrieved documents do **not** prescribe a bank-account verification procedure or say how to authenticate a changed account, so they do not answer that issue further.

4. **Ask for written confirmation of which payment method you are agreeing to use and any costs**, because the provider must tell you about costs associated with a particular payment method before you consent to use it. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf)

5. **Keep the request, confirmation and proof of payment**, and request a rent receipt if needed. For a non-personal payment, if you request a receipt when paying, it must be provided within **5 business days**; the receipt must state your name and premises, date, period covered, amount and that it is rent. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf)

6. **Check your bond separately**: the owner or agent must lodge it with the RTBA within **10 business days** after receiving it. The RTBA should send you a receipt; if you have not received one within **15 business days** after paying the bond, contact the RTBA at **rtba@justice.vic.gov.au** or **1300 137 164**. [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-06/21-3sra002%20authorised.pdf)

Based on the **Residential Tenancies Act 1997 (Vic), Authorised Version No. 088**, which was in force on 15 October 2019 [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf), here is what the law says about your situation:

### 🔑 Can you cancel?
The provided documents do not contain specific clauses detailing how to formally terminate or cancel a lease due to property defects. However, the Act does give you two immediate protections:
*   **Right to refuse entry:** A landlord must ensure the premises are vacant and in a reasonably clean condition on the day you are agreed to enter [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). You are **not required to move in** if these conditions are not met [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
*   **Rent protection:** If you choose not to move in, you are **not required to pay rent** for the period starting on your agreed move-in date and ending on the day you actually enter the premises [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).

### 🛠️ Can you ask for repairs?
Yes. The landlord has a strict duty to ensure the rented premises are maintained in good repair [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). Depending on the severity of the damp, mould, and rotting timber, you can pursue repairs through two pathways:

However, that regulation text comes from a 2026 version, so it doesn't establish what the 2019 standard said.

That is the version in force from 25 November 2025 to 2026-06-29, and its file name and metadata give it as version 111 [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). ## What the law says

- **Free method required (s 42(4)).** The provider or their agent must ensure that a rent payment method with no additional costs, other than your own bank or account fees, is reasonably available to you [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). A free bank transfer option is relevant here. The Act doesn't say whether a slower free method counts as "reasonably available", so I can't say it clearly does or doesn't.
- **Electronic payment facility charges (s 51(3)(b)).** A "person" must not demand or receive from a renter a charge for the establishment or use of direct debit facilities or any other electronic payment facility for paying rent [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). This isn't limited to the agent. If a card payment through the app is an "electronic payment facility", the rule could cover the payments company. The documents don't say whether it does.
- **Business fees on rent payments (s 51A).** A person carrying on a business must not demand or receive a fee for any *prescribed matter* relating to the payment of rent. The exceptions are the rental provider, the provider's agent, and authorised deposit-taking institutions (banks and similar) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
  - The payments company is none of those, so it isn't exempt.
  - The ban only applies to "prescribed matters". The retrieved Regulations extract (*Residential Tenancies Regulations 2021*, version 005, in force 25 November 2025 to 2026-02-09) doesn't list them [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf). I can't confirm whether a card fee is one.
- **Disclosure (s 42(7)).** Before you consent to a payment method, the provider or agent must tell you about any costs you may incur, including third party transaction fees and other electronic payment facility fees [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- **Standard form note.** The Regulations' form notes say the rental provider must permit a fee-free payment method, other than the renter's own bank fees [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf).

## Does it matter who gets the fee?

Yes, in part.
- Under s 51A, the agent and provider are exempt, but a separate payments company is not [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). A fee going to the app company is therefore more exposed than one kept by the agent. That still depends on the "prescribed matter" point above.
- Section 51(3)(b) refers to "a person" and doesn't depend on who receives the fee [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- The agent's own duties under s 42(4) and s 42(7) apply regardless of who collects the fee [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).

A later version of the Act (version 115, in force from 13 October 2026) substituted a different s 51A [[3]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/97-109aa115-authorised.pdf). It wasn't in force on 15 January 2026, so I haven't relied on it.

## What you can do

1. **Use the free bank transfer.** It avoids the fee entirely, and your own bank's fees are the only cost the Act allows for a no-cost method [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
2. **Ask the agent in writing** to confirm the cost of each payment method, including third party fees, as s 42(7) requires before you consent [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). Also ask them to confirm that a no-cost method is reasonably available to you, as s 42(4) requires [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
3. **Don't agree to the card fee** unless you're happy with it. The Act allows the payment method to be changed by agreement (s 42(6)), so it's your choice [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
4. **Check the prescribed matters** in the current Regulations, or get advice, if you want to challenge the fee. The retrieved documents don't cover that or say where to complain.

## Which law applies

On 15 October 2019 the version in force was the **Residential Tenancies Act 1997, Authorised Version 088** (*rta-1997-v088-2019-07-02.pdf*, in force 2 July to 3 December 2019) [[3]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). The extracts I retrieved from that version are endnote pages and don't include the operative text of the sections on handing over premises, repairs or rent. The operative text I found is in **Version 089** (*rta-1997-v089-2019-12-04.pdf*, in force from 4 December 2019) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/d98b58cd-fe91-3f90-92dd-3ce1ff4a6eb0_97-109aa089%20authorised.pdf). That is **later than your date**. I can't confirm from the documents that the wording was identical on 15 October 2019, so treat what follows as indicative only.

## What the law says

- **Handing over the premises.** On the agreed day the landlord must make sure the premises are "vacant and in a reasonably clean condition" (s 65(1)) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/d98b58cd-fe91-3f90-92dd-3ce1ff4a6eb0_97-109aa089%20authorised.pdf).
- **Not having to move in.** A tenant "is not required to enter into occupation of premises which do not comply" with that duty (s 65(2)) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/d98b58cd-fe91-3f90-92dd-3ce1ff4a6eb0_97-109aa089%20authorised.pdf). The documents don't say whether damp, mould and rotting timber count as not being "reasonably clean". That is the key question for this section.
- **Rent.** If the premises don't comply, you don't pay rent from the agreed move-in day until the day you actually enter into occupation (s 65(3)) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/d98b58cd-fe91-3f90-92dd-3ce1ff4a6eb0_97-109aa089%20authorised.pdf).
- **Repairs.** The landlord must ensure the premises "are maintained in good repair" (s 68(1)) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/d98b58cd-fe91-3f90-92dd-3ce1ff4a6eb0_97-109aa089%20authorised.pdf).

## What you can do

**1. Ask for repairs**
- **Urgent repairs (s 72).** You can arrange them yourself if you've taken reasonable steps to get the landlord or agent to do them immediately and couldn't. You must give 14 days' written notice of the repairs and their cost. The landlord must reimburse the reasonable cost, up to $1000 [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/d98b58cd-fe91-3f90-92dd-3ce1ff4a6eb0_97-109aa089%20authorised.pdf).
- **Tribunal for urgent repairs (s 73).** You can apply if you can't meet the cost, the repairs cost more than $1000, or the landlord refuses to pay. The Tribunal must hear the application within 2 business days [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/d98b58cd-fe91-3f90-92dd-3ce1ff4a6eb0_97-109aa089%20authorised.pdf).
- **Non-urgent repairs (s 74).** Give the landlord written notice. If the repairs aren't done within 14 days, you can apply in writing to the Director to investigate [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/d98b58cd-fe91-3f90-92dd-3ce1ff4a6eb0_97-109aa089%20authorised.pdf). Section 75 allows a Tribunal application, but my extract cuts off before the details [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/d98b58cd-fe91-3f90-92dd-3ce1ff4a6eb0_97-109aa089%20authorised.pdf).
- **What counts as "urgent".** The retrieved text doesn't define it, so I can't say whether mould or rot qualifies.

**2. Ask for lower rent**
- Under s 65(3) you owe no rent for the period before you move in, if the premises don't comply [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/d98b58cd-fe91-3f90-92dd-3ce1ff4a6eb0_97-109aa089%20authorised.pdf).
- Separately, the Tribunal must declare rent excessive if it is more than a tenant should reasonably pay, having regard to "the state of repair and general condition of the rented premises" (s 47(3)(b)) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/d98b58cd-fe91-3f90-92dd-3ce1ff4a6eb0_97-109aa089%20authorised.pdf). The Tribunal can order a refund of the difference (s 48) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/d98b58cd-fe91-3f90-92dd-3ce1ff4a6eb0_97-109aa089%20authorised.pdf). The start of s 47, including who can apply and when, is cut off in my extract.

**3. Cancel the lease**
- **Landlord's notice (Version 090).** The only termination provision for unfit premises that I found in a version close to your date lets the **landlord** give a notice to vacate if the premises are "unfit for human habitation" (s 245, Version 090, *rta-1997-v090-2020-03-02.pdf*, from 2 March 2020) [[4]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2020-02/97-109aa090%20authorised.pdf).
- **Tenant's notice.** A **renter's** right to give notice of intention to vacate for premises "unfit for human habitation" (s 91ZD) appears only in the amending text in the Version 088 endnotes [[3]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). In that text the party is called a "renter" and the other party a "residential rental provider". The documents don't show that this was in force on 15 October 2019.
- **Result.** I can't say from these documents whether you can cancel on that basis, or what a tenant's termination right for this problem was at that date.

## Gaps

For a definite answer on cancelling, and on whether mould and rot fall within s 65, check the Version 088 operative text. The Consumer Affairs Victoria or VCAT guidance current at that date would also help. Those materials weren't in what I retrieved.

**Short answer:** The retrieved documents don't say you must be home, and they don't say the agent can charge a $90 rebooking fee. They also don't contain the entry-rights sections as they stood on 3 December 2025, so some of this is indicative only.

## Which version applies
On 3 December 2025 the Act in force was *rta-1997-v111-2025-11-25.pdf* (version 111, in force from 25 November 2025) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). The Regulations in force were *rt-regs-2021-v005-2025-11-25.pdf* (version 005) [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf).

The retrieved extract of version 111 stops at around section 71. It does not include the entry provisions (ss 85–91A) [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf). The only text of those sections I found is in *rta-1997-v101-2022-09-07.pdf* (version 101, dated 7 September 2022) [[3]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). That is an earlier version, so treat what follows as a guide and not as the law in force on 3 December 2025.

## What the law says
- **Smoke alarm duty (version 111):** The rental provider must make sure each smoke alarm is working and has batteries. It must also be tested at least every 12 months. Testing a mains-powered alarm must be done by a suitably qualified person [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/97-109aa111-authorised.pdf).
- **Entry rights (version 101 text only):** The provider or agent may enter with the people needed for the purpose. For entry to carry out a duty under the Act, they need at least 24 hours' notice, and entry must be between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. on a day that isn't a public holiday [[3]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). Your 7 days' notice and 10 am–12:30 pm window fit within that.
- **Notice form (version 101 text only):** The notice must be in writing, say why they want to enter, and be given by post or delivered personally between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. [[3]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). Check yours meets this.
- **Manner of entry (version 101 text only):** Entry must be in a reasonable manner. People must not stay longer than needed without your consent [[3]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- **Your duty (version 101 text only):** You must permit entry that follows these rules [[3]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). The Regulations' standard-form summary also says you must allow entry where the rental provider has followed proper procedure [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf).

**Do you have to be there?** In the text I retrieved, your duty is to "permit" entry [[3]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). Nothing there says you must be present. Nothing there addresses an agent entering with a key while you are out either. I can't confirm from these documents whether either is allowed.

**Can they charge $90?** I found no provision about rebooking or missed-appointment fees. I tried two further searches on this and both failed, so this is a gap in what I could retrieve. It is not proof that no such rule exists.

## What you can do
- **Ask the agent in writing** what legal basis they rely on for requiring your presence and for the $90 fee. Ask them to confirm the entry would happen within the notice terms.
- **Check the notice** for the stated reason, written form, and delivery method [[3]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- **Go to the Tribunal if needed.** Under the version 101 text, you can apply to the Tribunal to limit when entry may occur [[3]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). If an entry doesn't comply with the entry rules, you can apply for an order restraining further entry for a set period [[3]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). Entering without complying, without reasonable excuse, is an offence [[3]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- **Contact Consumer Affairs Victoria** to confirm the current rules. The Regulations list their number as 1300 55 81 81 [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-11/21-3sra005-authorised.pdf).

Its metadata gives Version 101, in force from 7 September 2022 to 23 May 2023 [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). The text I retrieved does not print the words "Authorised Version No.", so I am taking the number from the file name and metadata. I also used the *Residential Tenancies Regulations 2021*, "rt-regs-2021-v002-2022-06-01.pdf" (1 June 2022), Version 002, in force until 30 November 2024 [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-06/21-3sra002%20authorised.pdf).

## What the law says

- **Where and how rent is paid:** Rent is payable at the place specified in the agreement, or at the premises if none is specified. It is payable in the manner specified in the agreement [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). The rental provider and renter may change how rent is paid only "by agreement" [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). Check what your signed agreement says about payment details, because a change of account is a change to the agreed payment manner.
- **A fee-free option:** The provider or their agent must make a payment method with no extra costs available. Your own bank fees are not counted as extra costs [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- **Costs information:** Before you consent to a payment method, you must be given information about any costs, such as third-party transaction fees or direct debit dishonour fees [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- **Receipts:** If you pay without handing over cash in person and ask for a receipt when you pay, the person who receives the rent must give you a written receipt within 5 business days [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). The receipt must be signed by the person receiving the payment. It must state your name and the premises, the date, the period covered, the amount, and that it is for rent [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). If no receipt is required, the recipient must keep a record for 12 months. If you ask for a copy, they must give it to you within 5 business days [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
- **Changed contact details:** The standard rental agreement form says the rental provider must notify the renter within 7 days if the provider's or agent's details change [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-06/21-3sra002%20authorised.pdf). This is a note in the prescribed form. It applies if your agreement is on that form (Form 1), and I can't tell that from your question.
- **Your bond:** If the agent is no longer involved, check the bond. Under Part 10, "residential rental provider" includes the provider's agent [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
  - The provider or agent must complete a bond lodgment form with you at the time you pay, and give you a copy once you sign it [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
  - They must pay the bond to the Residential Tenancies Bond Authority within 10 business days of receiving it [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
  - Until it is paid to the Authority, they hold it on trust for you [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
  - The Authority must send you a receipt within 7 days of receiving the bond [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
  - If you have no Authority receipt within 15 business days of paying, you may notify the Authority [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf). The lease form gives the contact details as rtba@justice.vic.gov.au or 1300 13 71 64 [[2]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-06/21-3sra002%20authorised.pdf).

## What you can do or ask

1. Ask for the change in writing, with the owner's full name and contact details. Compare these with the details in your signed agreement.
2. Check your agreement's payment clause. If it specifies an account or method, you don't have to agree to a different one, though you may agree to a change [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
3. Ask what costs, if any, the new payment method involves, and whether a fee-free option is available [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).
4. Ask for written receipts for each payment, and ask for them at the time you pay so the 5-business-day deadline applies [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2022-09/97-109aa101%20authorised.pdf).

You are **not required to enter into occupation** if they do not meet that requirement, and you are **not required to pay rent from the agreed occupation day until the day you actually enter into occupation**. [[9]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf)
- The rental provider must maintain the premises **in good repair**. [[9]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf)
- Mould or damp **caused by or related to the building structure** is included in the Act’s definition of an **urgent repair**. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf)
- The Act does **not**, in the retrieved provisions, state an automatic right to cancel or rescind a signed lease merely because defects are discovered before moving in. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf)[[9]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf)

## What you can do or ask

1. **Do not move in until the condition is addressed.** Give the rental provider or agent written notice immediately, describing the damp, mould and rotting timber. Keep dated photographs, videos and copies of all communications. The Act requires notice of damage to be given as soon as practicable. [[9]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf)

2. **Ask for urgent repairs.** If the mould or damp is structurally caused, or the rotting timber makes the property unsafe, ask the provider to arrange immediate repairs. If you cannot get the provider or agent to act, the Act permits a renter to arrange urgent repairs after taking reasonable steps to have the provider do them. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf)[[9]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf)

3. **Seek an order for repairs.** For non-urgent repairs, give written notice. If the provider has not completed them within **14 days**, you may apply to the Director to investigate and may apply to the Tribunal for an order requiring specified repairs. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf) For urgent repairs, you may apply to the Tribunal if you cannot meet the cost, the repairs exceed the prescribed amount, or the provider refuses to pay. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf)

[[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf) Do not stop paying rent without an agreement or Tribunal order; instead, after giving repair notice, you may apply for an order allowing rent to be paid into the **Rent Special Account** while repairs remain outstanding. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf)

5. **Ask the provider to agree in writing to end the lease and refund any bond or rent paid.** The retrieved documents do not say that the provider must agree, nor do they set out a specific pre-occupation cancellation procedure. [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf)[[9]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf)

- **No rent until you can move in.** If the premises don't comply, the tenant doesn't have to pay rent from the agreed occupation day until the day they actually enter occupation [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- **Duty to maintain good repair.** The landlord must ensure the premises are maintained in good repair [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).

## Your options

**1. Cancel (terminate the lease)**
- The tenancy terminates if the tenant has not entered possession and gives the landlord a notice of termination on the ground that the premises are not in good repair, are unfit for human habitation, or are unavailable for occupation [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).

**2. Ask for repairs**
- **Urgent repairs:** You may arrange urgent repairs if you have taken reasonable steps to get the landlord to carry them out immediately and the landlord can't be reached or doesn't act. The landlord must reimburse the reasonable cost, or $1000, whichever is less, after 14 days' written notice of the repairs and cost [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). You can also apply to the Tribunal (VCAT) for an order requiring urgent repairs. The Tribunal must hear it within 2 business days [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- **Non-urgent repairs:** Give the landlord written notice that repairs are required. If they aren't carried out within 14 days, you may apply to the Director to investigate [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). You can then apply to the Tribunal within 60 days of receiving the Director's report [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). The Tribunal can order the landlord to carry out specified repairs and specify the time for completion [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).
- The excerpts don't say whether these repair routes work before you have moved in.

If it makes such an order, the landlord cannot require rent above that amount for 12 months [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf). The Tribunal can also order a refund of the difference [[1]](https://content.legislation.vic.gov.au/sites/default/files/b45d24ec-5984-3225-b9f1-f61b16fc197c_97-109aa088%20authorised.pdf).

- Whether damp, mould and rotting timber are a breach of the duty to maintain good repair in your case.
- Whether the repair and rent processes apply before you move in.
- Bond, compensation and any amounts you have already paid.
